title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (previous page). On a ringed space X we are given two complexes of O_X-modules K', K''. We are also given an abelian sheaf G and a right G-torsor P. The data are:
- u : P → Hom^0(K',K''), whose sections are local chain maps;
- v : G → Hom^0(K',K''), additive;
- h : G → Hom^{-1}(K',K''), additive.
These satisfy u(pg) = u(p) + v(g) (written multiplicatively in the manuscript) and v(g) = d h(g) + h(g) d. In words: locally, each choice p ∈ P gives a chain map u(p) : K' → K''. Two choices differ by v(g), which is null-homotopic via a homotopy h(g) that depends additively on g. The goal is a single global morphism K' → K'' in the derived category D(X), even though P may have no global section. One then wants the induced map RΓ(X,K') → RΓ(X,K''), compatible with the Γ(X,O_X)-structure, and eventually a relative version over a morphism X → T.

The trick. Encode P as an extension 0 → G → Ḡ → Z → 0 whose fibre over 1 is P; this is the usual dictionary Ext^1(Z,G) = H^1(X,G) = {G-torsors}. Let L = [G →i Ḡ], placed in degrees −1 and 0 on this page (the previous page writes L^0, L^1; only the indexing differs). Since i is injective with cokernel Z, the projection gives a quasi-isomorphism L → Z.

The chain map. Define φ : L → H := Hom^•(K',K'') by:
- φ^{-1} = h;
- φ^0 : Ḡ → H^0, specified by its restrictions to G (namely v) and to P (namely u). The universal property of Ḡ is that Hom(Ḡ,F) = {pairs (v : G → F, u : P → F) with u(pg) = u(p) + v(g)}.
The square commutes, φ^0∘i = v = δh = δ∘φ^{-1}, which is exactly the homotopy condition. The condition δ^0∘φ^0 = 0 holds because the u(p) are chain maps. Hence φ is a morphism of complexes.

Passing to D(X). We get Z ≃ L → H. Tensoring with O_X (derived, or simply using the O_X-module structure of H) gives O_X → H. Composing with the canonical map H = Hom^•(K',K'') → RHom(K',K'') gives O_X → RHom(K',K'') in D(X). Applying RΓ gives RΓ(X,O_X) → RHom(K',K'') (global). Taking H^0 and the image of 1 ∈ Γ(X,O_X) gives an element of R^0Hom(K',K'') = Hom_{D(X)}(K',K''), the desired morphism.

Purpose. This is the abstract gluing lemma needed when a morphism of complexes exists only locally. The typical case in this dossier (Cartier operator / Gauss–Manin) is defining a map via local liftings, for instance of Frobenius, that differ by strictly additive homotopies.
errors: Notational slip: the page writes 'φ^0 i = u' and 'u = δk = δφ^{-1}'. On G the restriction of φ^0 is v, not u, so this should read φ^0∘i = v = δh. Also 'k' is the homotopy called h on the previous page.
Degree indexing of L shifts between pages: L^0, L^1 on the previous page versus degrees −1, 0 here. This is harmless.
Gap, not stated explicitly: one must assume each u(p) is a cocycle (a chain map) so that δ^0φ^0 = 0. This is implicit in the setup.
Gap, not stated explicitly: tensoring L with O_X should be derived, or one should simply use the O_X-linear extension of Z → H, since G and Ḡ need not be flat. The conclusion is unaffected.

The page does not discuss how the resulting morphism depends on the choice of (v,h), nor the obstruction picture: the class of P in H^1(X,G) pushed into H^1 of Hom^{-1}. This is left unfinished, and the page is the last of the folder.

ideas.what: Encoding a G-torsor P as the extension 0→G→Ḡ→Z→0 with fibre P over 1, and as the two-term complex [G→Ḡ] quasi-isomorphic to Z
ideas.modern_name: Ext^1(Z,G) ≅ H^1(X,G); torsors as extensions / Picard-stack style two-term complexes
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Grothendieck, Giraud; Deligne in SGA4 XVIII for Picard stacks)
ideas.where_published: Torsors/extensions: SGA 7 VII, Grothendieck's Tohoku-era torsor formalism; also SGA4 XVIII (Deligne)

ideas.what: Gluing locally defined chain maps, indexed by a torsor and differing by strictly additive homotopies, into a global morphism in the derived category via a chain map [G→Ḡ] → Hom^•(K',K'')
ideas.modern_name: Torsor-twisted gluing of homotopies; the mechanism behind Deligne–Illusie's gluing of local Frobenius-lift maps
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne–Illusie 1987 (Čech version); Mazur/Katz/Berthelot-type gluing of local Frobenius lifts earlier

ideas.what: Producing the morphism as the image of 1 under RΓ(O_X) → RHom(K',K''), giving automatic compatibility with the Γ(O_X)-module structure and a relative version over X→T
ideas.modern_name: Global sections of the internal RHom; morphism attached to a section of RHom

missed.claim: The data (torsor P, u : P→Hom^0, additive v, additive homotopy h with v = dh+hd), glued through the complex [G→Ḡ], is exactly the structure later used by Deligne–Illusie (1987). There the torsor is that of local liftings of Frobenius, and the additive homotopy h(F̃1,F̃2) glues the local quasi-isomorphisms φ_F̃ into a decomposition of F_*Ω^•. Grothendieck's version is Čech-free: it replaces the Čech argument with a two-term complex attached to the torsor's extension class. In this folder (Cartier operator, Gauss–Manin, c.1972–81) it plausibly served a similar Frobenius/Cartier gluing purpose.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This gives a clean, choice-free formulation of 'gluing along a torsor of lifts' that generalizes immediately to the relative setting over T. It anticipates the torsor-theoretic packaging later found in Ogus–Vologodsky and in the Deligne–Illusie literature. It is only a historical precedent, though, not a new theorem.

missed.claim: The relative version (over a morphism X→T) and the dependence of the morphism on (v,h) are announced but not worked out on the surviving pages.
missed.quote: et plus gén. en relativisant par rapport à un morphisme d'espaces annelés X → T
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. The relative version follows routinely from the same construction with Rf_*.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is a correct and elegant but essentially standard homological lemma. Its interest is historical: it is a Čech-free torsor-gluing device in a Cartier-operator dossier, structurally identical to what Deligne–Illusie used later. That is mildly notable, not revolutionary.
transcription_corrections: 'φ^{-1} = k': k denotes the homotopy h of the previous page.
'φ^0 i = u' should read φ^0 i = v (the manuscript's own slip). 'u = δk' likewise refers to v = δh.
Previous page 'G →v Hom^·(K'',K'')' is almost certainly Hom^0(K',K'').
'Tensorisant avec O_X, on trouve O_X ≃ (dans cat. dérivée) → H → RHom(K',K'')': the crossed-out symbol before H is likely L ⊗ O_X.
Last line: 'un élément de R^0Hom(K',K''), i.e. un homom de la cat. dérivée' (from K' to K'').
